items.claim: The prescript 1Cor.1.1-1Cor.1.3 has no finite main verb in the Byzantine text: the sender is a nominative, the adscript runs on participles (rp:1Cor.1.2 τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ; rp:1Cor.1.2 ἡγιασμένοις ἐν χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ) and the greeting rp:1Cor.1.3 χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη is verbless. The row's 'change of main verb' at 1:4, and its rejected alternative's 'distinct main verbs', therefore misstate the contrast: the first finite verb of the letter is the thanks verb at rp:1Cor.1.4 Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου πάντοτε. The seam after 1:3 and its high confidence stand; only the stated warrant is imprecise. No morphology layer is staged, so the verbless reading is this reviewer's reading of the forms.
items.both_sides: Before the seam, 1:1-1:3 is a verbless prescript (sender, adscript, greeting) closed by the greeting. After it, 1:4 opens asyndetically with the letter's first finite verb, the thanks formula, which both witnesses read alike in its opening words (sbl:1Cor.1.4 Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ). Nothing links 1:4 back to 1:3. The seam holds from both sides; the merge 1:1-1:9 is rightly rejected.

suggested_fix.fact: the prescript 1:1-1:3 is verbless (nominative sender, participial adscript, verbless greeting); the seam rests on the asyndetic onset of the letter's first finite verb, the thanks formula

items.claim: Both seams of 1Cor.1.4-1Cor.1.9 are borne by the Greek. The onset is the asyndetic thanks formula at 1:4. The close is the faithfulness clause rp:1Cor.1.9 Πιστὸς ὁ θεός, and 1:10 opens with the appeal formula rp:1Cor.1.10 Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, a new speech act (petition after thanks), so the vocative there does not stand alone (D4). The row subordinates its pilcrow wording ('the seam rests on the verb'). Its SBL claim is right: the critical sign at 1:4 stands before the possessive (sbl:1Cor.1.4 ⸀μου), and 1:4-1:9 hold no RP/SBL difference verse.
items.both_sides: Before 1:10, the period ends on God's faithfulness and the call into fellowship, with no connective to what follows. After, 1:10 carries the light particle de, but the appeal verb with its object and vocative opens the letter body. The rival close at 1:8 is rightly rejected: 1:9 grounds the confidence of 1:8.

suggested_fix.fact: no change: the seams rest on the thanks formula at 1:4 and the appeal formula at 1:10

items.claim: medium_low and the frontier flag are right for the hinge at 1Cor.1.17. In both witnesses 1:17 opens with gar (rp:1Cor.1.17 Οὐ γὰρ ἀπέστειλέν) and 1:18 opens with gar as well (rp:1Cor.1.18 Ὁ λόγος γὰρ ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ), so the Greek links backward on both sides of 1:17 and does not choose between a seam at 1:16/1:17 and one at 1:17/1:18. The cross word joins 1:17 to 1:18 (rp:1Cor.1.17 ὁ σταυρὸς τοῦ χριστοῦ), while 1:17 still carries the baptizing infinitive of the recollection (rp:1Cor.1.17 βαπτίζειν). The row names both pulls and discloses the hinge.
items.both_sides: Side 1:16/1:17: 1:17 continues the baptism recollection by its infinitive and first person and is tied to 1:16 by gar. Side 1:17/1:18: 1:18 is tied back by gar and takes up the cross phrase that ends 1:17, restating it as a third-person thesis. Neither side offers an asyndetic onset; the RP pilcrow at 1:18 informs only.

suggested_fix.fact: no change: the 1:17 hinge is linked by gar on both sides (1:17 and 1:18 both open with it), so confidence stays medium_low with the frontier flag

items.claim: The close-seam wording in boundary_rationale, 'an imperative turns the argument' at 1Cor.1.26, states as a form a mood the form does not decide: rp:1Cor.1.26 Βλέπετε γὰρ τὴν κλῆσιν ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί is a second-person plural present form identical in indicative and imperative, no morphology layer is staged, and the WEB face renders it as an indicative ('For you see your calling'). It also carries gar, a link back to the maxim of 1:25. The seam after 1:25 still stands on the turn from third-person thesis to the readers' own calling (rp:1Cor.1.26 τὴν κλῆσιν ὑμῶν), so medium_low stands; only the stated warrant is a reading presented as grammar.
items.both_sides: Before the close seam, 1:25 ends the wisdom/folly contrast with a maxim introduced by causal hoti (rp:1Cor.1.25 Ὅτι τὸ μωρὸν τοῦ θεοῦ σοφώτερον), itself a link back to 1:24. After it, 1:26 links back by gar but addresses the readers in the second person about their calling. At the onset, 1:17/1:18 is linked by gar on both verses and is rightly flagged as frontier ground.

suggested_fix.fact: 1:26 opens with a second-person form of the seeing verb whose mood the form does not decide, joined by gar to 1:25 (the WEB renders it indicative); the close seam rests on the turn to the readers' calling

items.claim: The row's only onset warrant, 'imperative with vocative' at 1Cor.1.26 (repeated in boundary_rationale and in strongest_rejected_alternative as 'the new imperative and vocative'), rests on a mood the form cannot decide and on a vocative that cannot set a boundary alone (D4). rp:1Cor.1.26 Βλέπετε γὰρ is identical in indicative and imperative, no morphology layer is staged, and the WEB face reads it as an indicative ('For you see'). Its gar makes 1:26 a ground of the 1:25 maxim, so the onset is linked, not asyndetic. The seam has a textual warrant the row does not name: the shift from the third-person thesis of 1:18-1:25 to the second-person calling of the readers (rp:1Cor.1.26 τὴν κλῆσιν ὑμῶν). The close side is sound. Confidence medium can stand once the onset warrant names that person shift and marks the mood as the author's reading.
items.both_sides: Before 1:26, 1:25 closes the thesis with a causal maxim in the third person. After it, 1:26 continues with gar (a link) but addresses the readers in the second person about their own calling; the merge with 1:18-1:25 is a live rival on the particle and is answered by the person shift and by the citation that closes 1:31. At the close, 1:31 ends on a citation formula (rp:1Cor.1.31 καθὼς γέγραπται), and 2:1 opens with a first-person pronoun, an arrival participle and the vocative (rp:1Cor.2.1 Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί); there the vocative is backed by the shift of person and tense, so D4 is met.

suggested_fix.fact: the onset at 1:26 rests on the shift from third-person thesis to the readers' calling in the second person; the verb form is mood-ambiguous and joined by gar to 1:25, so the mood is the author's reading and the vocative is supporting only

items.claim: Both seams of 1Cor.2.1-1Cor.2.5 are borne by the Greek. The onset rp:1Cor.2.1 Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί opens a first-person singular recollection with a pronoun and arrival participle, so its vocative is backed by more than itself. At the close, 2:6 takes up the wisdom word of 2:5 (rp:1Cor.2.5 ἐν σοφίᾳ ἀνθρώπων, then rp:1Cor.2.6 Σοφίαν δὲ λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖς τελείοις) with adversative de, a lexical link, but turns from first-person singular recollection of the past to a first-person plural present claim among the mature. The row names that turn; the seam stands at medium. Reading the verb of 2:6 as present is this reviewer's reading of the form; no morphology layer is staged.
items.both_sides: Before 2:6, 2:5 closes the recollection on a purpose clause contrasting human wisdom with God's power, which is the stretch's point. After it, 2:6 links by de and by the wisdom word, so the merge 2:1-2:16 is a live rival; the change of person and number, of time frame and of audience (the mature) answers it. At the onset, 1:31 closes on a citation and 2:1 begins the recollection.

suggested_fix.fact: no change: the 2:5/2:6 seam is linked by de and the wisdom word and rests on the shift to a first-person plural present claim

items.claim: 1Cor.2.6-1Cor.2.16 is one argument and both seams stand. The rival cut at 2:9/2:10 is handled with the C5 difference disclosed: RP reads rp:1Cor.2.10 Ἡμῖν δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀπεκάλυψεν and SBL reads sbl:1Cor.2.10 ἡμῖν ⸀γὰρ ⸂ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ θεὸς⸃; either particle makes 2:10 answer the citation of 2:9, so the rejection of a cut at 2:10 holds in both witnesses. The close: 2:16 ends on rp:1Cor.2.16 Ἡμεῖς δὲ νοῦν χριστοῦ ἔχομεν, and 3:1 opens with rp:1Cor.3.1 Καὶ ἐγώ, ἀδελφοί, the same opening pattern as 2:1, turning to the readers. The spiritual word carries across the seam (rp:1Cor.2.15 πνευματικὸς; rp:1Cor.3.1 πνευματικοῖς), a link that the change of address answers.
items.both_sides: Before 3:1, 2:14-2:16 completes the spiritual/unspiritual contrast and ends on a first-person plural claim. After it, 3:1 turns to second-person address with a first-person singular pronoun and the vocative and applies the spiritual/fleshly contrast to the readers; the shared spiritual word links the two sides, but the address changes. The onset at 2:5/2:6 is assessed under W1-006.

suggested_fix.fact: no change: the step closes on the claim to the mind of Christ at 2:16, and 3:1 turns to the readers with pronoun and vocative

items.claim: The close warrant 'slogans and the charge of being fleshly' at 1Cor.3.4 holds in RP only. RP reads rp:1Cor.3.4 οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε and SBL reads sbl:1Cor.3.4 ⸂οὐκ ἄνθρωποί⸃ ἐστε; at 3:1 RP reads rp:1Cor.3.1 σαρκικοῖς and SBL sbl:1Cor.3.1 ⸀σαρκίνοις. The fleshly stem rings 3:1, 3:3 and 3:4 in RP but appears only at 3:3 in SBL. device_notes gives the SBL 3:4 reading without saying whether the close holds under it, and omits the 3:1 adjective from its difference list. The seam after 3:4 holds in both witnesses on the slogans of 3:4 and the turn to the two leaders at 3:5, so confidence medium stands.
items.both_sides: Before the seam, 3:1-3:4 diagnoses the readers and ends on the slogans that echo 1:12 and on the closing charge (fleshly in RP, merely human in SBL). After it, 3:5 opens with inferential oun in both witnesses (rp:1Cor.3.5 Τίς οὖν ἐστιν Παῦλος; sbl:1Cor.3.5 ⸀Τί οὖν ἐστιν) and carries over the two names of 3:4, so the Greek links across the seam, which the rejected alternative admits without naming the particle; the turn is from the readers' condition to what the leaders are.

suggested_fix.fact: the fleshly charge closing 3:4 is the RP reading (SBL reads 'not human' there and another fleshly adjective at 3:1); the seam holds in both witnesses on the slogans of 3:4 and the turn to the leaders at 3:5, which is linked by inferential oun

triage_answers.decision: No c01 row credits a layout mark with deciding, opening or closing a seam, and no boundary_evidence_refs entry cites one; no WEB paragraph or chapter division is credited anywhere in c01. W1-001 and W1-002 explicitly subordinate the pilcrow. W1-003, W1-004, W1-005 and W1-006 give location wording only. The nearest to 'supporting' is W1-007 boundary_rationale (span 1Cor.2.6-1Cor.2.16), 'A Byzantine pilcrow heads 2:6 as well', where 'as well' adds the mark to the onset case: reword to location wording. W1-005 boundary_rationale (span 1Cor.1.26-1Cor.1.31), 'Robinson-Pierpont prints a pilcrow at 1:26, where this step begins', is location wording; it stays acceptable only once the onset warrant is reworded (W1-005 item), since otherwise it is the clearest onset statement left in the prose. W1-008 mentions no mark.
